_comment: Words a parsed 'evidence needed' sentence may use to say HOW a reader
checks a criterion (the rubric parser's own contract: one sentence on
what a reader would look at) without adding to WHAT is required.
Complete-claim rules treat such evidence as a restatement only when every
word is the criterion's own, part of a whole section name, or listed in
'words'. 'comparison_words' may appear only when the evidence states the
same bound as the criterion (same kind, same numbers). Quantifiers such as
'all' or 'only' are deliberately absent: they can add a requirement. Any
other word keeps the evidence in the claim, so the rule abstains and the
criterion is graded with instructor review instead.
